Some filers publish tables or whole pages as images, so absence here is not proof of absence.","length":725889,"next_offset":582884,"offset":580389,"period":"2024-12-31","returned":2495,"text":"Junior Subordinated Debentures for one or more consecutive interest periods that do not exceed 10 years. Interest compounds during such deferral periods at the rate in effect for each period. The interest deferral feature obligates the Company in certain circumstances to issue common stock or certain other types of securities if it cannot otherwise raise sufficient funds to make the required interest payments. The Company has reserved 75 million shares of its authorized and unissued common stock to satisfy this obligation.
The terms of the Subordinated Debentures and Junior Subordinated Debentures prohibit the Company from declaring or paying any dividends or distributions on common or preferred stock or redeeming, purchasing, acquiring, or making liquidation payments on common stock or preferred stock if the Company has elected to defer interest payments on the Subordinated Debentures or Junior Subordinated Debentures, respectively, subject to certain limited exceptions.
In connection with the issuance of the Junior Subordinated Debentures, the Company entered into a replacement capital covenant (“RCC”). This covenant was not intended for the benefit of the holders of the Junior Subordinated Debentures and could not be enforced by them. Rather, it was for the benefit of holders of one or more other designated series of the Company’s indebtedness (“covered debt”), currently the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due in 2053. Pursuant to the RCC, the Company has agreed that it will not repay, redeem, or purchase the Junior Subordinated Debentures on or before May 15, 2067 (or such earlier date on which the RCC terminates by its terms) unless, subject to certain limitations, the Company has received net cash proceeds in specified amounts from the sale of common stock or certain other qualifying securities. The promises and covenants contained in the RCC will not apply if (i) S&P upgrades the Company’s issuer credit rating to A or above, (ii) the Company redeems the Junior Subordinated Debentures due to a tax event, (iii) after notice of redemption has been given by the Company and a market disruption event occurs preventing the Company from raising proceeds in accordance with the RCC, or (iv) the Company repurchases or redeems up to 10% of the outstanding principal of the Junior Subordinated Debentures in any one-year period, provided that no more than 25% will be so repurchased, redeemed or purchased in any ten-year period.

content.text:
Allstate's FY2024 10-K (Note 14, Capital Structure) shows one junior subordinated issue outstanding at December 31, 2024: **$500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures**. The balance was the same $500 million a year earlier, at December 31, 2023.

**Maturity**
- The scheduled maturity date is May 15, 2057.
- The final maturity date is May 15, 2067. The debt table lists the issue as "6.500% Junior Subordinated Debentures, due 2067."

**Interest**
- Until May 15, 2037, interest is fixed at 6.500% and paid semi-annually.
- After that it floats and is paid quarterly. The original rate was three-month LIBOR plus 2.120%. LIBOR has been replaced by the three-month CME Term SOFR Reference Rate plus a spread adjustment of 0.26161%, so the effective rate is Term SOFR + 2.120% + 0.26161%.

**Redemption**
- On or after May 15, 2037, Allstate can redeem all or part of the issue at any time, at principal plus accrued and unpaid interest.
- Before May 15, 2037, it can redeem all or part only in certain circumstances. The price is principal plus accrued and unpaid interest or, if higher, a make-whole price.

**Interest deferral**
- Allstate can defer interest for one or more consecutive interest periods, up to 10 years. Deferred interest compounds at the rate in effect for each period.
- In certain circumstances, the deferral feature requires Allstate to issue common stock or certain other securities if it cannot otherwise raise enough money to pay the interest. It has reserved 75 million authorized but unissued common shares for this.
- While interest is deferred, Allstate generally cannot declare or pay dividends or distributions on its common or preferred stock. It also cannot redeem, buy, acquire or make liquidation payments on that stock. There are some limited exceptions.

**Replacement capital covenant (RCC)**
- Allstate entered into an RCC when it issued the debentures. The covenant protects holders of a designated "covered debt" series, currently the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053. Holders of the junior subordinated debentures cannot enforce it.
- Under the RCC, Allstate will not repay, redeem or buy back the debentures on or before May 15, 2067 (or an earlier RCC termination date) unless it has received net cash proceeds in specified amounts from selling common stock or other qualifying securities. Certain limitations apply.
- The RCC does not apply if any of the following happens:
  1. S&P upgrades Allstate's issuer credit rating to A or above.
  2. Allstate redeems the debentures because of a tax event.
  3. A market disruption event after a redemption notice prevents Allstate from raising the proceeds the RCC requires.
  4. Allstate repurchases or redeems up to 10% of the outstanding principal in any one-year period, with no more than 25% in any ten-year period.

**Sources**
- Allstate Corp Form 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-02-24, accession 0000899051-25-000015 (Note 14, Capital Structure).
